new_statements.quote: L'accent en qawasqar a tendance à reposer sur l'avant-dernière syllabe. Néanmoins, il y a des exceptions et on ne peut pas toujours prédire la place de l'accent. On dira cependant qu'il y a dans cette langue certaines habitudes auxquelles on tient. C'est les cas où, dans nos exemples, on note la place de l'accent. Par ailleurs, dans beaucoup de cas on peut changer la place de l'accent sans que l'informateur en tienne compte. Plusieurs fois, nous avons eu l'impression qu'on prononçait les unités sans mettre en relief aucune syllabe ou, ce qui revient au même, en mettant en relief toutes les syllabes.
new_statements.translation: Accent in Qawasqar tends to rest on the penultimate syllable. Nevertheless there are exceptions and the place of the accent cannot always be predicted. One can say, however, that the language has certain habits that are adhered to; those are the cases where, in our examples, we mark the place of the accent. Moreover, in many cases the place of the accent can be changed without the informant taking any notice. Several times we had the impression that units were pronounced without any syllable being made prominent or, which comes to the same thing, with every syllable made prominent.

C'est les cas où, dans nos exemples, on note la place de l'accent. Par ailleurs, dans beaucoup de cas on peut changer la place de l'accent sans que l'informateur en tienne co…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No fixed position. Clairis (1977: 152; Spanish version 1978: 36): a tendency to penultimate stress, with exceptions, not always predictable, and freely movable without the speaker noticing; some words seem to have no prominent syllable at all. Aguilera (1978: 58), the other first-hand describer, says stress is 'free' (libre): it may fall on any of the last three syllables of thematic (uninflected) forms and shifts in compound/suffixed forms, its position being governed by rules based on the structure of the vowel nuclei and syllable groups that he promised to publish separately (never found here). Aguilera's later pedagogical statement (2012, quoted in Mineduc 2023: 99) calls it 'movible' and shows the shift under suffixation: jéksor 'see' but jeksór-fqat (monosyllabic suffix) vs jéksor-afqát.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Aguilera 1978: 58 marks 'un acento de menor intensidad' with a grave accent in some lexicon entries; the Mineduc/Aguilera 2012 text says only primary stress is. jéksor-afqát shows two marked peaks. No rule given.
new_statements.exceptions: Clairis: exceptions to the penult tendency are frequent and stress can shift without effect; Salas 1996 (after Aguilera 1982/83): stress can move over the last three syllables (esdrújula/grave/aguda) without changing the word's meaning or perception, i.e. non-contrastive. Aguilera 1978: shifts in compound forms. The two primary describers disagree on whether there is a penult tendency (Clairis) or a rule-governed three-syllable window (Aguilera).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (unité lexicale / palabra); Clairis's data are elicited citation forms from Puerto Edén speakers (northern/Puerto Edén variety); Aguilera's 'formas temáticas' vs 'formas compuestas' distinguishes bare stems from suffixed verb forms. Stress placement is written with an acute accent in the official Kawésqar orthography.
new_statements.identity_note: All statements concern the Puerto Edén (northern, 'alacalufe septentrional') variety, the only one with modern speakers; Clairis and Aguilera worked with the same Puerto Edén community in the 1970s. Glottolog qawa1238 covers the whole language; no separate glottocode for the northern dialect is used here. Note two rival phoneme analyses (Clairis 23 vs Aguilera 26 phonemes), but stress statements do not depend on that.

readall_conflicts: Among the material already held by the project in our check folder for this language (downloaded 2026-09-17 by the earlier reading, re-verified here in the saved text files), the sources disagree in emphasis but not in substance: Clairis 1977 (La Linguistique 13, p. 152; catalog's existing statement) says stress tends to fall on the penult but with exceptions and is not always predictable; Aguilera 1978 (Boletín de Filología 29, p. 58 = the text layer) says 'Respecto al acento, sea brevemente dicho, es libre en Kawésqar, puede caer en las tres últimas sílabas en las formas temáticas y sufrir desplazamientos en las formas compuestas. Su posición está regulada por reglas que funcionan de acuerdo a la estructura de los núcleos vocálicos y los grupos silábicos' (free within the last three syllables, shifts in compounds, rules promised but unpublished); and Aguilera 2012 as quoted in the Mineduc 3º Básico programme (p. 99, the text layer) says 'El acento en kawésqar es movible.. jéksor (ver).. jeksór-fqat.. jéksor-afqát' (mobile, shifts under suffixation, only primary stress marked). Aguilera's 'free/mobile within a three-syllable window, with structure-dependent rules' is compatible with Clairis's 'penult tendency with exceptions'; no source gives a fixed position, so the best-supported reading is lexically unpredictable (free) stress, possibly weight-conditioned per Aguilera's unpublished rules. Aguilera 2001 is the work most likely to state those rules and remains unread.
